newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends near session lows, seen sideways.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends near session lows, seen sideways.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures ended up but near session's lows on Tuesday, floor traders said.
The market had gained some strength from good roaster and trade support. Origin selling dried up as the market dipped below $1,800 basis September.
But it peaked in the afternoon on firmer New York due to talk around the floor about the possibility of a cold front bringing cooler temperatures to Brazil.

"New York's behaviour is good," said one. The September arabica futures cleared the immediate 170 cents/lb resistance to hit a high of 171.75 but slipped back to hold at just 169.25 at 1553 GMT, still 3.55 cents higher.
But private U.S. forecaster WSC said the coming week should see continued warm, high pressure dominating Brazil's coffee belt.
"Harvest weather will be quite favourable," it said in its latest update.
September gapped $20 higher as expected but headed to a high of $1,822 a tonne before finishing the day $8 up at $1,785. Its low-point was $1,762.
Traders said the market was likely to continue to trade sideways in low volume, with prices ambling within a $100 price band.
"There's some buying at $50 below and selling at $50 higher than current levels," said one.
Chartwise, the London market was seeking a break on either side. Analysts said if anything, there's a little pressure on the downside.
Initial support is seen at $1,755, Monday's low, followed by the June 11 low of $1,695.
A break of $1,695 would see a move down to $1,550, the lows not seen since early April.
